title: Phoenix Active Management Area Fifth Management Plan — Phase 65 TSMC Arizona delivery review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the TSMC Arizona delivery reporting pack. The Phoenix AMA Fifth Management Plan establishes conservation, monitoring, reporting, variance, audit, and compliance requirements for municipal, agricultural, and industrial groundwater users in the fifth management period.
key_findings: ADWR states that the fifth plans were adopted in 2022 and that their conservation requirements became effective January 1, 2025, remaining in effect until the legislature determines otherwise.
The plan includes industrial programs for large-scale power plants, large-scale cooling facilities, mining, and new large industrial users, alongside general monitoring and reporting requirements.
Implementation provisions cover compliance dates, water measurement, records, annual reports, audits, inspections, variances, administrative review, and plan modifications.
why_it_matters: Which records separate campus construction, utility arrangements, workforce inputs, qualification, customer acceptance, and repeat facility output? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. The plan converts broad Arizona water constraints into inspectable sector and compliance requirements relevant to industrial growth in the Phoenix region.
ftfn_relevance: Adds an enforceable policy layer to the U.S. Southwest Chip Corridor's water evidence stack.
Defines the area-wide regulatory context for industrial cooling, power, mining, and new large industrial users.
Identifies compliance, reporting, variance, and audit records that can become later project-specific evidence.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
Area-wide conservation rules do not prove a named project's water right, allocation, utility capacity, service agreement, actual use, compliance, or reclaimed-water infrastructure.
The plan cannot substitute for provider, permit, agreement, facility, or operating records.
The publication date is represented at year precision because the official landing page provides adoption-year and effective-date context rather than a single document issue date.
